card.summary: 2 GB file storage on the Free plan (10 users, unlimited spaces and pages). Crucially: 'Free, Standard, and Premium plans entitle you to one app instance. You...

free_tier.stated: 2 GB file storage on the Free plan (10 users, unlimited spaces and pages). Crucially: 'Free, Standard, and Premium plans entitle you to one app instance. You can have as many of these plans as you need. You'll subscribe to each one separately.' Each instance 'will have its own storage'.

egress.terms: No egress meter anywhere in Atlassian Cloud pricing. Attachments are served from the site domain, not a billed CDN bucket.

record.tooling: Confluence Cloud REST API v2/v1 (`/wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment`), Basic auth with email + API token, or OAuth 2.0. No rclone backend; the API is the client.
record.chaining: 2 GB x N free Confluence sites, and N is self-service and explicitly unbounded ('as many of these plans as you need'). Ten free sites = 20 GB; a scripted site-creation loop is the multiplier. Community reports confirm multiple free sites per account are allowed and the one-instance limit is a paid-plan construct.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: attachment default 100 MB, admin-configurable upward ('Enter your preferred maximum size (in bytes)'). Quota is per-site, not per-org. request-rate: Atlassian Cloud REST rate limits apply. Retention: Free sites are DEACTIVATED after a period of inactivity (logging in and viewing a page counts as activity). This is the real hazard, not eviction. Over-quota does not delete data, it restricts editing/creating.
record.reliability_note: Nothing is deleted at quota. Writes are blocked until you upgrade or free space. But a Free site that goes untouched is deactivated, so a storage-only site needs a periodic login to stay alive.

record.provider: Atlassian Confluence Premium via Social Impact (nonprofit) License — unlimited file storage

free_tier.stated: Confluence Premium = 'Unlimited file storage'. Atlassian's Feb 2026 announcement grants eligible nonprofits and social enterprises 100% off Confluence 'Standard or Premium up to 25 users' under the Social Impact License. So a verified nonprofit gets a 25-seat Confluence Premium site with no storage cap, for free.

per_object_cap.stated: per-object-cap is the binding constraint: 'The default size limit is 100 MB

egress.terms: No egress meter on Confluence attachment downloads. Attachments are served from api.media.atlassian.com / the site's CDN with no bandwidth line item in the plan comparison.

record.tooling: Confluence Cloud REST API v1/v2 (POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment, GET .../child/attachment, GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/download/attachments/{filename}); community CLI wrappers exist (github.com/nlink-jp/confl-cli, github.com/eddieland/confluence-dl, github.com/justmiles/go-confluence). No rclone backend.
record.chaining: 'Unlimited' is per Confluence site; each site is one org. Multiply by creating many spaces inside one site (unlimited spaces even on Free), and by the number of verified nonprofits. Premium edition also removes the 250 GB Standard ceiling for the same $0. The licence tier is the multiplier, not the seat count.

limits.value: per-object-cap is the binding constraint: 'The default size limit is 100 MB

record.limits_note: Per-object-cap is the binding constraint: 'The default size limit is 100 MB' per attachment, and Atlassian's own migration doc says the limit 'can be configured for Legacy editor pages, but not for the default editor' (feature request CONFCLOUD-72157 still open). So 20 TB = ~200,000 objects of <=100 MB. request-rate: Atlassian does not publish a Confluence Cloud REST request rate on these pages — unverified; the storage page itself is only refreshed 'every 4 hours'. retention: none published; archiving a page does NOT free storage because Atlassian 'stores all attachments for version history purposes'. Deletes are the only way to reclaim.
record.reliability_note: Free Confluence sites can be deactivated for inactivity (login is the counter). Premium removes the storage cap but not the 100 MB object cap, and archived content is billed forever. Anonymous read of a public space works; anonymous write does not (probed: 200 read, 403 write).

card.summary: Free (up to 5 users): 1 GB LFS storage. Academic 5 GB, Standard 5 GB, Premium 10 GB. Extra storage sold in 100 GB units at $10/month. Notable counter-propert...

free_tier.stated: Free (up to 5 users): 1 GB LFS storage. Academic 5 GB, Standard 5 GB, Premium 10 GB. Extra storage sold in 100 GB units at $10/month. Notable counter-property: no per-file cap at all.

egress.terms: Not metered. Atlassian publishes no LFS bandwidth quota, only storage in 100 GB units. This is the one LFS host where the storage number is small but the transfer side is genuinely unstated/unbilled.

record.tooling: Git-lfs. Note: SSH not usable for LFS repos? (not stated). The documented limitation is that repository transfer and forking both break LFS links; the alternative route is `git lfs fetch --all` + `git lfs push --all`.
record.chaining: 1 GB per free workspace, unlimited free workspaces (each needs an email). 500 workspaces = 500 GB of very awkward storage. Weak: no route to manage many workspaces at once, and the workspace is tied to users.
record.limits_note: 'there's no limit on the LFS file size you can push to Bitbucket Cloud'. Genuinely no per-file cap. Forks do not copy LFS objects (fork points at parent's store, and the fork lacks permission). So fork-based sharding fails. Repo archives do not include LFS files.
record.reliability_note: Fork/transfer/archive are all documented as broken for LFS repos, which makes recovery awkward. Storage overage is auto-billed in 100 GB increments rather than blocked.

evidence.proved: 'Free (up to 5 users) | 1 GB'; '100 GB of file storage | Your monthly bill goes up $10'
